heading: Chap. iv.
paragraphs:
Let not the widows be overlooked; on account of[1391] our
Lord be thou their guardian, and let nothing be done without
thy will; also do thou nothing without the will of God,
as indeed thou doest not. Stand rightly. Let there be frequent[1392]
assemblies: ask every man [to them] by his name.
Despise not slaves, either male or female; but neither let
them be contemptuous, but let them labour the more as for
the glory of God, that they may be counted worthy of a more
precious freedom, which is of God. Let them not desire to
be set free out of the common [fund], lest they be found the
slaves of lusts.
